items.rationale: Two instructions need the same hardware unit and it can serve only one, which is a structural hazard. The second divide would wait even if it needed nothing from the first. Choosing a data hazard shows M3, that every stall is a data hazard.
The pipeline fetched before it knew the next address, because the branch outcome was not known yet: a control hazard. Choosing data hazard shows M3.
Ideal cycles are 5 + 6 - 1 = 10, and the 3 stall cycles add to 13. An answer of 10 forgets the stalls; 33 uses no overlap.
CPI = 1 + 0.25 x 2 = 1.5. An answer of 2.25 or 3 applies the penalty to every instruction, or forgets the base CPI of 1.

items.answer: Stalls also come from structural hazards (a shared resource) and control hazards (an unknown next instruction after a branch), not only data hazards.
accepted: There are also structural and control hazards
Stalls can also be caused by branches or by two instructions needing the same hardware
It ignores structural and control hazards
items.rationale: A full answer names at least one other cause, structural or control. A learner who defends the statement or adds only more data-hazard detail shows M3.
